source.title: Towards Binary-Valued Gates for Robust LSTM Training
source.authors: Zhuohan Li; Di He; Fei Tian; Wei Chen; Tao Qin; Li-Wei Wang; Tie-Yan Liu

record.tranche_reason: Compares a gate-training intervention with standard training and reports held-out task performance, but does not measure the train–test gap or test random-label fitting.
record.gate_note: Reports natural-data test perplexity and BLEU for G2-LSTM and comparison methods. It does not test arbitrary-label memorization, train–test gaps, or the conditions and measures specified by V1–V8. Cited work on flat minima and generalization is not this study's result.
record.test_reason: The study uses a flat-minima generalization rationale to motivate Gumbel-Softmax LSTM gates and reports its method's performance and compression robustness. It tests none of V1–V8: in particular, it does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness, training–test gaps, or their ranking against other generalization measures.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report improved or comparable task performance, greater robustness to gate-parameter compression, and more interpretable gates. They suggest better generalization as an explanation for the performance gains; they do not directly establish the proposed flatness mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Gumbel-Softmax gate sampling as a training intervention; evaluates language modeling and translation rather than random-label memorization or train–test gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report a performance drop when output gates are also pushed toward 0/1. They state temperature has no significant effect on results. Compression changes outcomes, but those measurements do not test the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: G2-LSTM achieves test perplexity 52.1 versus 52.8 and 53.2 with a continuous cache pointer, and BLEU 31.95 versus 31.00 and 29.73 on German→English and 22.43 versus 21.89 and 21.64 on English→German.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gumbel-Softmax training of LSTM input and forget gates can improve held-out language-modeling and translation performance relative to standard and sharpened-sigmoid gate training.

record.problems: The paper reports test metrics but not training errors or train–test gaps, so the reported performance comparisons cannot establish changes in generalization gap. No uncertainty estimates are stated for these comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: Compression results in Tables 3–5 compare robustness to parameter compression, not a measured generalization gap or a condition named in V1–V8; omitted.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and training recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning and recovery interventions.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce the large-batch penalty.
Controlled dropout comparisons and effects of training-set size, dropout strength, or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equal numbers of random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The decisive issue is the absence of comparisons measuring V1–V8, rather than the absence of training errors alone. Compression robustness measures held-out performance after structured parameter changes, not V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance measured through training error.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels under the same recipe.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test-error changes.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and tuning or recovery conditions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects on held-out error and the stated data-size and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to train–test gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: Baseline
rows.operation_detail: Trained standard LSTM without the Gumbel-Softmax trick; evaluated on Penn Treebank language modeling.
rows.note: The paper reports the test metric but does not report corresponding training error.
rows.check: 52.8 is AWD-LSTM with a continuous cache pointer, not without one. The without-cache test perplexity is 57.3. Table 1 attributes the baseline result to Merity et al.; Table 3 repeats 52.8 as the uncompressed baseline.
